declarations.name: ManagedSettingsStore
declarations.comment:
A data store that applies settings to the current user or device.

The Managed Settings data store groups settings according to function.
Each group contains relevant data about its associated settings,
for example, a default value and minimum and maximum possible values.

### Configure Settings

Use the settings objects to inspect your application's current configurations as well as apply new configurations.
Changing the value of a setting to `nil` deletes your app's configuration for that setting from the device.
The system doesn't guarantee that the settings you specify govern the device's behavior.
The system is responsible for determining its effective state based on all the settings it receives.

### Examine Effective Settings

In a few cases, you can also access the effective settings.
For example, a media app can access the effective rating settings to filter the content it offers,
even though it doesn't provide configurations for these or any other settings.
Subscribe to ``ManagedSettingsStore/$effectiveMaximumTVShowRating`` or
``ManagedSettingsStore/$effectiveMaximumMovieRating`` to determine what TV shows or movies to offer.

declarations.name: ShieldActionDelegate
declarations.comment:
A class for an extension that handles shield actions.

Subclass `ShieldActionDelegate` to allow client extensions to respond to user actions on a shield that covers an application or website.
The system doesn't provide the name of a shielded ``Application``, ``WebDomain``, or ``ActivityCategory``
to preserve the Family Sharing group's privacy.
Instead, the system uses a token to indicate what content it is shielding.

members.name: handle
members.signature: func handle(action: ShieldAction, for application: ApplicationToken, completionHandler: @escaping (ShieldActionResponse) -> Void)
members.comment:
Allows the extension to respond to a user action when the system displays a shield over an application.

- parameter action: The user's action.
- parameter application: The application that the shield covers.
- parameter completionHandler: A closure for your extension to call after you handle the user's action.

members.comment:
Allows the extension to respond to a user action when the system displays a shield over an application or website because of its category.

- parameter action: The user's action.

members.name: webDomains
members.comment:
Websites for the system to cover with a shielding view.

When the user visits a website in this list of domains,
the system calls your extension that customizes the shield’s appearance.
When the user taps on a button the shield displays,
the system calls your extension that handles user actions.
If your app doesn't provide a list of domains to shield, this value is `nil`.
Your app can shield up to 50 web domain tokens at once.

declarations.name: Token
declarations.comment:
A representation of an activity, such as an app or website, that doesn't reveal its identity.

Managed Settings uses a `Token` to preserve user privacy and prevent anyone
outside of a Family Sharing group from identifying what apps and websites the family accesses.
You can use tokens to restrict and filter device use without accessing personal information.

The ManagedSettings framework provides the following types of tokens:

- term ``ManagedSettings/ApplicationToken``: An opaque representation of a selected app.
- term ``ManagedSettings/WebDomainToken``: An opaque representation of a selected web domain.
- term ``ManagedSettings/ActivityCategoryToken``: An opaque representation of a selected category of activity.

members.name: blockedByFilter
members.comment:

The default value is ``WebContentSettings/FilterPolicy/none``, which indicates that the system doesn't block any websites.

members.name: blockedByFilter
members.comment:
The current policy for filtering websites.

Setting any filter policy besides `.none` will disable Safari private browsing.
The value is `nil` unless you specify a policy.
Your app can block up to 50 web domains and
specify up to 50 web domains exceptions at once.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Creates an object that represents the specified web domain.

Provide a high-level domain, such as `example.com`.
To protect a family's privacy, use ``init(token:)`` instead.
- Parameter domain: A website to allow or block.

members.name: domain
members.comment:
A string that identifies a specific web domain.

In an extension that provides shield configurations, this property provides the web domain.
When you access this property outside that extension, the value is `nil`.
See <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/ManagedSettingsUI/ShieldConfigurationDataSource> for more information.

declarations.name: WebDomainToken
declarations.comment:
A representation of a web domain that preserves the user's privacy.

Managed Settings uses representations of web domains to preserve user privacy and control.
Use a token to represent a web domain without revealing what domain the token represents.
<doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/FamilyControls/FamilyActivitySelection>
provides tokens that devices within the same Family Sharing group can use to identify applications.
